segments: 286 Chronography of Barhebraeus.
"and they must not spend the night outside,
because my spies have informed me
that the Franks are prepared to attack them."
However, Sinqur, since in his pride he was negligent and did not accept her advice,
seven hundred Frankish horsemen arrived
and attacked those Turks,
and only a very few of them escaped.
And after this,
she secretly and prudently sent Sinqur-Daraz with presents and gifts to the Emir Aqsunqur.
And he departed from her territory and went to Sarug,
and he fought against it for five days;
and the forces that were with him consumed its crops and its produce.
And from there he went to Shabakhtan,
and he held a great banquet.
And Malik Mas'ud, the son of the Sultan, came to him,
he who had remained in Harran,
and did not cross the Euphrates with Mawdud.
And there he imprisoned Ayaz,
the son of Ilghazi son of Artuq, the lord of Mardin,
and he also plundered the territory of Mardin.
And in this very year,
which is the year 1426
of the Greeks,
on the 29th of the latter Tishrin,
which was the 29th
of the sixth month of the Arabs,
there occurred an exceedingly severe earthquake,
in which {OCR?: that in it} the city of Mar'ash completely sank down,
and became a grave for its inhabitants.
And many courtyards also fell in Samosata.
And Constantine, the lord of Gargar, happened to be in it,
and he was suffocated in it along with many others.
And thirteen towers from the wall of Edessa fell,
as well as portions from the wall of Harran,
and a hundred courtyards in Balash, along with half of its citadel.
Also two churches of Kesum:
that of Mor John and that of the Forty Martyrs;
and through the diligence of Mor Dionysius, its bishop, they were rebuilt anew.
And in the year
509 of the Arabs,
which is the year 1427
1427 of the Greeks,
Roger, the lord of Antioch, with five hundred horsemen, attacked the Emir Aqsunqur Bursuqi {OCR?} at Ma'arra.
And he and Zangi, his brother, fled,
and he went up onto a certain hill.
And the Franks were occupied {OCR?: occupied themselves} with the slaughter of the force of the Turks,
and with the plundering of the merchants and market-folk who were with them.
And Aqsunqur and his brother fled with a small number of men,
and the Franks pursued them for about a parasang, but did not overtake them.
And they returned and took three thousand Turks captive.
And they broke the chests and the poles of the tents of the Turks,
and set them on fire.
